cards.subtitle: Deterministic Adhémar Jean Claude Barré de Saint-Venant (1871) & August Ritter (1892) shallow-water dam-break Riemann rarefaction law (conserving Riemann invariant R_+ = u + 2*sqrt(g*h) = 2*sqrt(g*h_res) across the centered expansion fan so the dry-bed flood wavefront advances at u_front = 2*sqrt(g*h_res) = 2*c_0*(1+u), locking u_exact / u_model = 1.0000x across all 17 reservoir-depth stations h/h_0 = (1+u)^2 in [1.000, 4.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive depth-invariant constant flood speed (u = 2*c_0, which underestimates front speed by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x / 4x energy at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-wave Riemann characteristic rarefaction fan quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Dam-break flood inundation, tsunami shoreline run-up, spilled bucket water spreading, and open-channel sluice gate animations
Driving the wet-dry flood front at u_front = 2 * sqrt(g * h_res) and the parabolic rarefaction surface profile h(x,t) = (1/(9g)) * (2*sqrt(g*h_res) - x/t)^2
Scaling upstream retreating depression wave speed at -sqrt(g * h_res) while the downstream dry tip advances twice as fast at +2*sqrt(g * h_res)
not_for: Deep-ocean dispersive Airy capillary-gravity waves where water depth h >> wavelength lambda
